name: "Discord"
description: "chat-community and server-discovery product design: Discord ships its real design-token layer - :root hue scales (--neutral-*, --blurple-*, --plum-*, the --*-new-* families, --illo-*, --opacity-*) plus class-scoped .theme-light/.theme-darker semantic blocks carrying --background-base-*/--background-surface-*/--background-mod-*, --text-*, --border-*, --badge-*, --button-* and --input-* - over a gg-sans + ABC-Ginto app that paints .theme-dark.theme-darker (#121214/#202024 bases, #efeff1 ink, #5865f2 blurple actions, rgba(151,151,159,0.16) selected fills, #43b581 online green, 2px #6aa8f4 focus rings) next to a Ggsans Webflow marketing shell (blurple gradients, 56px Nord display, pill CTAs); signed-out server discovery, a searchable category-tab card grid with member counts and verified badges, a /servers/<slug> detail with Join/Share, and the login/register auth cards"

# Discord

Generated from [tokens.json](tokens.json) and [README.md](README.md) by the design-systems catalog tool. Do not edit this file: change the tokens through the package's builders, then run `make design-md` at the repository root.

It follows the DESIGN.md spec, version alpha. That format has no themes, no per-value provenance and only px, em and rem units, so this file holds the `light` theme alone with every alias resolved. [tokens.json](tokens.json) is the source of truth: it records where each value was read, holds the `dark` theme, and keeps the 29 tokens from these groups that DESIGN.md cannot hold (gradients, shadows, percentages, durations and other non-colour or non-px values).

## Overview

Good for: chat-community and server-discovery product design: Discord ships its real design-token layer - :root hue scales (--neutral-*, --blurple-*, --plum-*, the --*-new-* families, --illo-*, --opacity-*) plus class-scoped .theme-light/.theme-darker semantic blocks carrying --background-base-*/--background-surface-*/--background-mod-*, --text-*, --border-*, --badge-*, --button-* and --input-* - over a gg-sans + ABC-Ginto app that paints .theme-dark.theme-darker (#121214/#202024 bases, #efeff1 ink, #5865f2 blurple actions, rgba(151,151,159,0.16) selected fills, #43b581 online green, 2px #6aa8f4 focus rings) next to a Ggsans Webflow marketing shell (blurple gradients, 56px Nord display, pill CTAs); signed-out server discovery, a searchable category-tab card grid with member counts and verified badges, a /servers/<slug> detail with Join/Share, and the login/register auth cards.

Captured 2026-11-15, read-only (the marketing pages, /servers discovery + categories, /servers/<slug> details, /login and /register are public signed out; the whole client - /channels/*, joining servers, invites, messages, settings - is an authenticated boundary never reached; every button and field was measured, never submitted or followed). Themes: light, dark.

A token set and component reference for Discord's public surface — for building chat-community apps, server-discovery grids, auth cards and marketing heroes in the style of the real thing. It was read from **discord.com** on **2026-11-15**, signed out, in headless Chromium at 1440 x 900 and 390 x 844. Captured: the marketing pages (/, /download, /nitro), the server-discovery pages (/servers, /servers/gaming), a /servers/<slug> detail page, the /login and /register auth cards, and 390px passes on the home page and discovery.

Discord is worth a capture because it ships its real design-token layer to the browser — and because the site is two products in one. The marketing pages are a Webflow build in Ggsans/ABC Ginto over the brand palette; the app surfaces run the real Discord design system: "gg sans" body text, "ABC Ginto Discord Nord" display type, `:root` hue scales (`--neutral-1..100`, `--blurple-1..100`, `--plum-0..26`, the `--*-new-1..100` families, `--illo-*`, `--opacity-*`, `--brand-*`, `--primary-*`) and class-scoped semantic blocks `.theme-light`/`.theme-darker`/`.theme-dark`/`.theme-midnight` carrying `--background-base-*`/`--background-surface-*`/`--background-mod-*`, `--text-*`, `--border-*`, `--badge-*`, `--button-*`, `--input-*`. 4,469 variables resolve per theme — and unlike most products, both themes really paint signed out: app surfaces carry `.theme-dark.theme-darker` while the marketing chrome injected into them sits under a `.theme-light` root. The app paints a `#121214`/`#202024` base with `#efeff1` ink, `#fbfbfb` strong text, `#5865f2` blurple on Join/Log In (`#4752c4` hover), `rgba(151,151,159,0.16)` selected pills, `#43b581` online green and 2px `#6aa8f4` focus rings; the auth card is an oklab `#26282c`-ish panel on the animated brand backdrop. **Boundary:** the whole client needs an account — /channels/* redirects to /login, invites are not accepted, and joining, sharing, and Nitro purchase gate on sign-in; every button was measured, never pressed. The app's standalone light surface (the account theme setting) and `.theme-dark`/`.theme-midnight` variants are declared but unpainted signed out.

## Do's and Don'ts

- Do take values from [tokens.json](tokens.json) when you need another theme, a value's source, or a token this file leaves out.
- Do read [README.md](README.md) before relying on a value; it says what is known to be wrong.
- Don't read colours off the screenshots; they are 256-colour PNGs.
- Don't copy the product's logo, icons, illustrations or brand colours into something that ships. Borrow structure and proportions.
- Don't edit this file; it is regenerated from the tokens.
